Package bakerydms

Class BakeryOrderWindow

  • java.lang.Object
    • bakerydms.BakeryOrderWindow
  • public class BakeryOrderWindow
extends java.lang.Object
    The main window of the program and the only screen the user works with (the presentation layer).

    The window has five areas:

    • Database bar - server, port, database, username, password and Connect.
    • Order form - Add, Update, Delete and Clear for one order.
    • Order table - every order in the database, with Search, Show All and Refresh.
    • Report bar - the Daily Production Report (the custom action).
    • Status bar - the result of the last action, green or red.

    The window never stores or checks data itself. Every action is passed to OrderManager, which validates it with OrderValidator and saves it through the OrderRepository that DatabaseConnector opened. Each button handler runs inside safely(...), so a database error or an unexpected problem is shown in a message box and the program keeps running. Typed values are checked before anything is saved: problems are listed in a message box and the matching fields are outlined in red.

    Usage (this is what BakeryApp does): 

    
 BakeryOrderWindow window = new BakeryOrderWindow(manager, new DatabaseConnector());
 SwingUtilities.invokeLater(window::show);
    Version:
    4.0 (Phase 4, Module 11)
    Author:
    Kayla Ewing
    See Also:
    OrderManager, Theme

      • connectToDatabase

        public boolean connectToDatabase()
        Connects to the MySQL database using the details in the database bar. Blank or badly formatted details are reported before connecting; a wrong password, an unknown server or a missing database are reported after trying. Nothing here can crash the program.
        Returns:
        true if the database was connected and its orders loaded

      • refreshFromDatabase

        public boolean refreshFromDatabase()

        Throws:
